what_it_does: When an AI model starts fresh on a GPU—whether in serverless computing, spot instances, or edge devices—there is a significant delay before it can actually run. This delay comes from loading the actual GPU code (like from NVIDIA's cuDNN library) onto the GPU before execution. PASK solves this by pre-loading code objects before the model is invoked and intelligently reusing the same code across different neural network layers, avoiding redundant loads. The system overlaps code loading with actual computations so the loading happens 'behind the scenes' rather than causing visible startup delay.
